route_note: llama.cpp's own CMake build of the test-backend-ops target at the exact commits (buggy 0b14b87d7c, fixed 9bd4c09ea5), identical flags for both variants: cmake (system 3.26.5, accepts CUDA 13.4) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 (derived from $RW_NVCC_FLAGS; ggml turns it into --generate-code=arch=compute_89,code=[compute_89,sm_89], SASS + PTX) -DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS=-lineinfo -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_SERVER=OFF -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DLLAMA_SUBPROCESS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH='$ORIGIN', no -G, `cmake --build --target test-backend-ops -j8` (8 min per variant). One deviation from the defaults: -DLLAMA_SUBPROCESS=OFF, because the first attempt failed to compile common/subproc.cpp: vendor/sheredom/subprocess.h:1215 'error: posix_spawn_file_actions_addchdir_np was not declared in this scope' (that call needs glibc >= 2.29, the cluster has 2.28; the vendored header of this older commit is unguarded; the newer 9e0e220 of llamacpp-2 is guarded). The option only removes subprocess support from llama-common and does not touch test-backend-ops or any CUDA code. Project Release nvcc flags kept: -lineinfo -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++17 -use_fast_math -extended-lambda -compress-mode=size. Relocatability: ggml/llama are static libraries so all device code is in the test-backend-ops executable; the gcc-12.4 runtime libs libstdc++.so.6, libgcc_s.so.1, libgomp.so.1 are copied next to it and found through the $ORIGIN rpath (system libstdc++ is gcc 8, no static libstdc++.a exists); libcudart/libcublas/libcublasLt through RPATH /usr/local/cuda-13.4/targets/x86_64-linux/lib, libcuda.so.1 from the driver. Checked with env -i ldd and env -i ./test-backend-ops --help from BeeGFS. -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF builds the CPU reference backend for baseline x86-64 so the binary runs on any node. Source tarball: 2,071 files (CMakeLists.txt cmake common ggml include licenses src tests vendor examples pocs app tools without tools/ui).
